title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Marine-Pollutant Surcharge
content:
## What this governs

Goods declared under Dangerous Goods Acceptance as marine pollutant carry, once loaded, a marine-pollutant surcharge of their own. The desk books it as one marine-pollutant entry on the acceptance's dangerous-goods account, distinct from the hazardous-cargo surcharge entry; the account then shows the charge, dated the day it was booked, and a higher balance.

## Tool reference: `book_dg_marine_pollutant_surcharge_a7ecff71`

**Effect.** A call records one marine-pollutant charge on the acceptance's dangerous-goods account, stating how many containers it was computed on, and adds the amount to the acceptance's outstanding charges. Sending the identical call again produces no second charge and no change in the balance.

**Getting to it.** The tool is hidden. The agent unlocks it first, using the unlock facility for agent tools, and then runs the call itself.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `dg_id` | the dangerous-goods acceptance whose marine-pollutant goods were loaded, as the acceptance lookup shows it | identifier |
| `charge_code` | tariff code of the entry; accepts one value only, `marine_pollutant_surcharge`; the `dg_surcharge` entry and all other dangerous-goods charges cannot be booked here | enumerated |
| `container_count` | containers the charge is computed on | whole number |
| `amount_usd` | the charge to book | US dollars, 2 decimals, rounded half up to the cent beforehand |

**Receipt.** On success: `dg_event_id` of the new charge, `dg_id`, `charge_code` reading `marine_pollutant_surcharge`, `container_count` charged, `amount_usd` booked, and `charges_due_usd` after the charge, to 2 decimals.
